learning_outcomes.text: Students should know the parts of an MPCS (manufacturing planning control system).
Students should know where an MPCS is located within the logistics chain.
Students should know planning and production control systems such as MRP, MRP II, JIT in more detail.
Students should be able to measure management using key indicators or KPIs.
Know the techniques for planning, scheduling, and production control.
Apply business organization strategies, techniques, and tools based on the structures and resources of the company.
Able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.
Able to become aware of the multidisciplinary nature of industrial engineering, as well as its social, economic, and environmental implications.

syllabus_topics: Presentation of the course, students and professor
assessment_rules: The continuous assessment (EC) score is based on four partial written exams, each contributing 20% to the final grade (total 80%). Class presentations combined with Excel assignments contribute the remaining 20% to the continuous assessment. If the continuous assessment score is 5 or higher, the course is passed with a 5. To improve the grade, students may take the ordinary exam, which then averages 50/50 with the continuous assessment; if this average is below 5, the final grade will be 5. If the average between continuous assessment and the ordinary exam is below 5, but the ordinary exam score is above 5, the final grade is 5. For the extraordinary (resit) exam, if the course was not passed in the ordinary call, the extraordinary exam score accounts for 50% of the final grade, and the continuous assessment score for the other 50%. If the average between continuous assessment and the extraordinary exam is below 5, but the extraordinary exam score is above 5, the final grade is 5.
